why: No hyperscaler has cut 2027 plans, but cracks are showing. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says Google is cutting 2027 shipments of a Broadcom-designed AI chip by about a fifth (neither company has commented), and Alphabet sold bonds at wider spreads than in May. After the Democratic sweep, UBS says ~30% of expected 2028 US data-centre additions could be at risk from construction pauses. Spending is still debt-funded, with free cash flow negative at three of the four biggest spenders.

Chip stocks gave back part of Monday’s surge on Tuesday: Nvidia fell 5.9% to US$155.38, Micron 11%, AMD about 9% intraday and the chip index nearly 6% intraday. Nvidia is still about a third below its October record, its board’s investigation continues, a congressional probe is under way, and Reuters has reported SEC staff are examining possible accounting issues (no finding of wrongdoing).

A 25 bp hike on 9 Dec is about 95–97% priced, and markets give about 59% odds of another in January (24 Nov). Consumer confidence hit its highest in nearly two years, which supports the hawks. October PCE inflation lands at 12:30am Thursday 26 Nov Melbourne time.

No newer default-swap figures have been published since Friday 20 Nov, when Oracle’s protection rose to about 328 bp (above the 300 bp bursting threshold) and CoreWeave’s to about 1,233 bp. CoreWeave shares fell 11.9% on Tuesday after Monday’s 22% jump, and Oracle slipped more than 2% intraday. ETFs that would bet against CoreWeave, Oracle and Meta debt have been filed with the SEC.

Anthropic closed at US$81.91 on Tuesday, down 6.5% and below its US$83 IPO price for the first time (intraday low US$75.61). Analysts cited its capital needs, the lack of a credit rating so far and profit-taking. It has committed about US$900bn to computing over two decades. Nvidia’s US$118bn of customer guarantees, about US$105bn tied to one OpenAI campus, remains in focus. (Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic.)

Roughly flat at about 4.92% on Tuesday after dipping just under 4.9% (a two-week low) during the day. Stocks were mixed rather than falling across the board, so the bursting pattern of yields falling sharply while stocks fall is not present.
US crude rose 2.35% to settle at US$82.05 on Tuesday, snapping a three-week losing streak; Brent was about US$90.66. Oil remains well above pre-war levels, keeping inflation pressure on the Fed.
High-yield spread 323 bp on 13 Nov (320 bp on 12 Nov): broad credit is still calm. IMF: US bank loans to non-bank lenders rose 18% in 2026.

Tuesday split the market: the Nasdaq fell 1.5% on chip losses while the Dow rose 0.9% to a record above 50,000 and small caps rose 0.6%. The S&P 500 slipped only 0.5%. That is a tech-led pullback, not tech and the broad market falling together.
